19 An object is stretched until it reaches the elastic limit.
Which statement must describe the stress on the object when it is at the elastic limit?
A
It is the maximum stress for which the object obeys Hooke’s law.
B
It is the maximum stress that can be applied to the object before it has elastic deformation.
C
It is the maximum stress that can be applied to the object before it has plastic deformation.
D
It is the maximum stress the object can withstand before it breaks.

hints: Notice the wording asks for the elastic limit, not the limit of proportionality for Hooke's law and not the breaking point.
Recall the difference between elastic deformation that recovers fully on unloading and plastic deformation that leaves permanent extension.
Test each statement against that difference: decide which one marks the boundary between reversible and permanent deformation.
walkthrough: Identify what is given: the object is stretched just to the elastic limit, so if unloaded now it would still return to its original length.
State the governing idea: below the elastic limit all extension is elastic and reversible; above it some extension is plastic and permanent.
Check Hooke's law: proportionality of $stress$ to $strain$ can end at the limit of proportionality, which may be below the elastic limit, so it does not define the elastic limit.
Check fracture: breaking requires the stress at which the material separates, which comes after the plastic region and is not the elastic limit.
Conclude that the elastic limit stress is the maximum stress before permanent plastic deformation starts. This is option C

A.explanation: This describes the limit of proportionality, where $stress \propto strain$ stops. Hooke's law can fail before the elastic limit is reached.

B.explanation: Elastic deformation occurs from small stresses upwards and is reversible. The elastic limit is not the start of elastic behaviour.

C.explanation: This is the definition of the elastic limit: the largest stress with fully reversible deformation, beyond which permanent plastic deformation remains.

D.explanation: This describes the breaking stress at fracture. Fracture occurs after extensive plastic deformation, well beyond the elastic limit.
